newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom mulling directory service charges.
newsitem.headline: Telecom mulling directory service charges.

text.p: Telecom Corp said on Friday it was struggling to cope with the number of directory service calls while holding down costs and was mulling a charging regime.
Such a charge, if it was introduced, would be offset by a reduction in line rentals. Telecom said 85 percent of customers would pay less overall.

Spokesman Clive Litt said Telecom did not believe such charging affected the Kiwi share, which put conditions on Telecom including the provision of free local calling when the government sold Telecom in 1990.
Telecom said there had been exponential growth in directory service use recently, with many of those local inquiries.
Litt said Telecom decided against making a charge for directory service because it "did not want to see this as an opportunity to increase our earnings".

"The problem is that there has been a huge increase in demand for Directory Assistance over the past five years and this growth is projected to continue at the same rate in the future," Telecom said in a statement.
Growth in calls this year has been at a rate of 28 percent.
